name: Double pendulum chaos (bench)
prompt:
Build ONE self-contained HTML file that simulates TWO identical double pendulums side by side on a single <canvas data-testid="simulation">. Use the real equations of motion for a double pendulum (Lagrangian form or equivalent), g = 9.81, integrated with a FIXED timestep that only advances when driven (see BENCH.step) or by your own requestAnimationFrame loop during free viewing. Pendulum B starts with theta1 offset by exactly 1e-3 radians from pendulum A; everything else identical. Draw fading trails for both bobs, plus a live readout of the divergence.

MANDATORY benchmark API — a hidden automated grader calls exactly this; it must exist on window before load finishes, be deterministic for a given seed, and be independent of wall-clock time:
window.BENCH = {
  reset(seed) {},            // re-init both pendulums deterministically; seed 1 => default initial angles (theta1 = 2.0 rad, theta2 = 0.5 rad, zero velocities, B offset by +1e-3 on theta1)
  step(ms) {},               // advance BOTH pendulums by exactly ms milliseconds of simulated time using fixed-dt substeps
  perform(action, payload) {}, // support 'setTheta1' with payload {rad: number} applied to pendulum A while at rest
  getState() { return {seed, timeMs}; },
  getMetrics() { return {timeMs, angle1A, angle1B, divergence, energyDriftPct}; }
};
divergence = |angle1A - angle1B| in radians at the current simulated time. energyDriftPct = |E(t) - E(0)| / |E(0)| * 100 for pendulum A (total mechanical energy).

Use EXACTLY these equations of motion (point masses m1, m2; rod lengths l1, l2; angles t1, t2 from vertical; angular velocities w1, w2; den = 2*m1+m2-m2*cos(2*t1-2*t2)):
a1 = (-g*(2*m1+m2)*sin(t1) - m2*g*sin(t1-2*t2) - 2*sin(t1-t2)*m2*(w2*w2*l2 + w1*w1*l1*cos(t1-t2))) / (l1*den)
a2 = (2*sin(t1-t2)*(w1*w1*l1*(m1+m2) + g*(m1+m2)*cos(t1) + w2*w2*l2*m2*cos(t1-t2))) / (l2*den)
Integrate with RK4 or semi-implicit Euler at fixed dt <= 5 ms. Do NOT re-derive physics — implement the above. Reason briefly (a few paragraphs max); the COMPLETE file must fit in your output.

Also include <button data-testid="reset">Reset</button> wired to BENCH.reset(1). No external libraries — plain canvas 2D and vanilla JS only.
notes: Chaos, made measurable: a 1e-3 rad initial offset must grow to >= 0.05 rad divergence within 10 simulated seconds, and energy drift <= 5% guards against unstable integration. step() is wall-clock independent, so grading is deterministic and identical across models.
